english_title: Lemma in the Fourier Transform Version
statement_en: If $f \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, and its Fourier transform is defined by $$\hat{f}(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}f(x)e^{-2\pi i x \cdot \xi } \, dx,$$ then $$|\hat{f}(\xi)|\to 0 \text{ as } |\xi| \to \infty.$$ Since the Fourier transform of an integrable function is continuous, this is essentially the statement that $$f \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n) \implies \hat{f} \in C_0(\mathbb{R}^n).$$
prerequisites: continuity of the Fourier transform of integrable functions
callout_body:
如果$f \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$,其傅里叶变换:
$$\hat{f}(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}f(x)e^{-2\pi i x \cdot \xi } dx$$那么$$|\hat{f}(\xi)|\to 0 \text{ as } |\xi| \to \infty$$
因为[[可积函数的傅里叶变换是连续的]]，那么这个命题实际上就是证明$$f \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n) \implies \hat{f} \in C_0(\mathbb{R}^n)$$
